native_context: HTTP response header structure and CRLF handling
taxonomy_note: Planning compatibility lens only. Classify the final observed root cause independently; unsupported mappings stay unassigned.

controls.boundary: HTTP response header structure and CRLF handling — authoritative consumer
controls.source_trace: Trace untrusted input to the response-header API and actual serialized HTTP version/server stack. Separate header value validation from log or body rendering.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an isolated local client/server with an inert marker. Inspect raw serialization for the exact suspected line-boundary input and compare a normal header value. Determine whether extra headers/messages are actually emitted, rejected or encoded by the framework.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Control characters in application logs are not wire-level response splitting. A client display artifact or an HTTP/1 hypothesis does not establish behavior over a different protocol stack.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Use supported header APIs and reject prohibited characters at the serialization boundary. Retest legitimate values and the original serialized anomaly on the affected stack.

coverage_unit: One primary investigative assertion for this technique; not exhaustive coverage. Expand only for genuinely distinct policy/effect assertions in the actual assessment.
